canonicalName: Arithmetization of analysis and the construction of the real numbers

milestones.label: Dedekind devises cuts (unpublished)
milestones.description: Dedekind worked out his definition of real numbers by cuts of the rationals but kept it private for years.

evidence.claim: Cuts were worked out in 1858 and published only in 1872.

milestones.label: Weierstrass lectures on real numbers (unpublished)
milestones.work: Weierstrass, Berlin lectures from 1865 (not published at the time)
milestones.description: Weierstrass gave his own theory of the real numbers in Berlin lectures that circulated through students, not in print.

evidence.claim: His theory was given in lectures beginning in 1865 and not published.

milestones.note: Lecture-based precursor; the theory reached print via students such as Hankel and later editions.

milestones.label: Meray publishes an arithmetical theory of irrationals
milestones.work: Meray, Remarques sur la nature des quantites definies par la condition de servir de limites a des variables donnees, Revue des Societes savantes, 1869
milestones.description: Meray defined irrational numbers as limits of convergent rational sequences, the first such theory to appear in print.

evidence.claim: Cited as the first published arithmetical theory of irrational numbers (1869).

milestones.note: Original journal not located in Crossref; year rests on MacTutor. Hankel 1867 is described as proposing the change of viewpoint, not a construction.

milestones.label: Heine's construction by fundamental sequences
milestones.work: E. Heine, Die Elemente der Functionenlehre, J. reine angew. Math. 74, 1872
milestones.description: Heine built real numbers from Cauchy-type rational sequences with arithmetic and order, following Cantor's idea.

evidence.claim: Crossref lists the paper in volume 74 (1872).
Heine introduced arithmetic operations and an order on his sequences.

milestones.label: Cantor's real numbers from fundamental sequences
milestones.work: G. Cantor, Ueber die Ausdehnung eines Satzes aus der Theorie der trigonometrischen Reihen, Math. Ann. 5, 1872
milestones.description: Cantor defined real numbers as classes of rational Cauchy sequences within a paper on trigonometric series.

evidence.claim: Crossref records the paper in Math. Ann. 5 (1872).
Cantor published a version in 1872 using Cauchy sequences of rationals.

milestones.label: Dedekind's cuts published
milestones.work: R. Dedekind, Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen, Braunschweig: Vieweg, 1872
milestones.description: Dedekind published his definition of the reals by partitions of the rationals, showing continuity without geometric appeal.

evidence.claim: Archive.org record: Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen, Vieweg, 1872.
Dedekind published after realising Heine and Cantor were about to.

milestones.label: Pierpont titles a survey 'On the arithmetization of mathematics'
milestones.work: J. Pierpont, On the arithmetization of mathematics, Bull. AMS 5, 1899
milestones.description: A survey carrying the name of the programme in its title; an earlier coinage by Kronecker is mentioned but undated here.

evidence.claim: Crossref records the article in Bull. AMS 5 (1899).
Kronecker is said to have introduced the term, later shifted in meaning.

milestones.note: Earliest coinage not established; Kronecker (e.g. 1887, Ueber den Zahlbegriff, Crelle 101) and Klein (1895) are candidates, not verified as first use.

milestones.label: Landau's Grundlagen der Analysis
milestones.work: E. Landau, Grundlagen der Analysis, 1930
milestones.description: A textbook building naturals, rationals, reals and complexes step by step from Peano axioms.

evidence.claim: Contemporary review in Amer. Math. Monthly 37 (1930).

milestones.note: Dated from a review; not the first systematic treatment of the construction, but a standard one.

works.citation: Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen, 1872
Ueber die Ausdehnung eines Satzes aus der Theorie der trigonometrischen Reihen, Math. Ann. 5
Remarques sur la nature des quantites definies par la condition de servir de limites a des variables donnees
Die Elemente der Functionenlehre, Crelle 74

notes: Priority is spread: Meray (1869) is first in print, Weierstrass and Dedekind earlier in private. Weierstrass's lectures are undated beyond 'from 1865'. Hankel 1867 not verified in a record. Naming milestone is low confidence; Kronecker's coinage and Klein's 1895 address were not verified.

canonicalName: Riemann's zeta function and the prime number theorem
aliases: Prime number theorem (Hadamard, de la Vallee Poussin)
phases: Proof of the prime number theorem

milestones.label: Euler's zeta function over the reals
milestones.description: Euler studied the zeta series and its product over primes for real arguments, linking primes to analysis.

evidence.claim: Euler used the zeta function with real argument as early as 1737.

milestones.label: Chebyshev's partial results
milestones.description: Chebyshev, using real zeta values, showed the prime counting ratio is bounded above and below and that any limit must equal one.

evidence.claim: Two papers from 1848 and 1850 attempted the asymptotic law.

milestones.label: Riemann's memoir on the number of primes
milestones.work: B. Riemann, Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grosse, Monatsberichte der Berliner Akademie, 1859
milestones.description: Riemann continued zeta to the complex plane and tied its zeros to the primes, proposing complex methods for counting primes.

evidence.claim: The 1859 memoir connects the primes to zeros of the continued zeta function.
Crossref records the memoir reprinted in the Gesammelte Werke (original year from the citation).

milestones.note: The reprint record carries no 1859 date; the year comes from the journal citation on the history page.

milestones.label: von Mangoldt proves Riemann's formula
milestones.work: H. von Mangoldt, Zu Riemanns Abhandlung 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grosse', Crelle 114, 1895
milestones.description: von Mangoldt gave rigorous proofs of the explicit formula suggested by Riemann, preparing the ground for the final proof.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Crelle 114 (1895), title referencing Riemann's memoir.

milestones.note: Description of content from the title and background knowledge; not read in the paper.

milestones.label: Hadamard proves the prime number theorem
milestones.work: J. Hadamard, Sur la distribution des zeros de la fonction zeta(s) et ses consequences arithmetiques, Bull. SMF 24, 1896
milestones.description: Hadamard showed zeta has no zeros on the line Re s = 1 and deduced the asymptotic law for primes.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Bull. Soc. Math. France, 1896.
Both 1896 proofs use complex analysis and non-vanishing on Re s = 1.

milestones.label: de la Vallee Poussin's independent proof
milestones.work: C.-J. de la Vallee Poussin, Recherches analytiques sur la theorie des nombres premiers, Ann. Soc. Sci. Bruxelles 20-21, 1896
milestones.description: An independent proof in the same year, with a later 1899 memoir adding an error term.

evidence.claim: Proved independently of Hadamard in 1896.
Hadamard and de la Vallee Poussin proved it in 1896.

milestones.note: No Crossref record found; Wikipedia gives the Brussels citation.

milestones.label: Landau's Handbuch der Lehre von der Verteilung der Primzahlen
milestones.work: E. Landau, Handbuch der Lehre von der Verteilung der Primzahlen, Leipzig: Teubner, 1909
milestones.description: A two-volume treatise collecting the analytic theory of primes, including the complex-analytic proof.

evidence.claim: Archive.org record dated 1909.

works.citation: Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grosse
works.whyItMatters: continuation of zeta and link to primes

works.citation: Sur la distribution des zeros de la fonction zeta(s)
Recherches analytiques sur la theorie des nombres premiers
Zu Riemanns Abhandlung

notes: Riemann's date is cited from journal references, the reprint record has no original year. Hadamard and de la Vallee Poussin are simultaneous. Naming ('Riemann zeta function') and an MSC/institution entry (11M) were not dated here. Later simplifications (Selberg and Erdos 1949, Newman 1980) are outside the scope.

canonicalName: Vortex atoms and the origin of knot tabulation

milestones.label: Helmholtz on vortex motion
milestones.work: H. Helmholtz, Ueber Integrale der hydrodynamischen Gleichungen, welche den Wirbelbewegungen entsprechen, Crelle 55, 1858
milestones.description: Helmholtz showed vortex filaments in an ideal fluid persist and can form closed rings.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Crelle 55 (1858).
Helmholtz showed vortex cores are filaments forming rings, with no link to matter theory.
evidence.source: Wikipedia, Vortex theory of the atom

milestones.label: Thomson proposes vortex atoms
milestones.work: W. Thomson, On vortex atoms, Phil. Mag. 34, 1867
milestones.description: Thomson proposed atoms as stable knotted vortex rings in the aether, so that kinds of knot would give kinds of atom.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Phil. Mag. (4) 34 (1867), 'On vortex atoms'.
Published in Proc. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh in 1867 per the history page.
evidence.source: Wikipedia, Vortex theory of the atom

milestones.note: The Proc. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh volume 6 is dated 1869 in Crossref; the paper itself dates from 1867.

milestones.label: Tait's first paper On Knots
milestones.work: P. G. Tait, On Knots, Trans. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh 28, 1877
milestones.description: Tait took up the knot question raised by vortex atoms and began enumerating knots.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Trans. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh 28 (1877), 'On Knots'.
Tait was drawn in by Thomson's idea and began a classification of knots.

milestones.note: Volume 28 spans 1876-78; Tait's first communication may predate the printed year.

milestones.label: Kirkman's enumeration of knots
milestones.work: T. P. Kirkman, The enumeration, description and construction of knots of fewer than ten crossings, Trans. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh 32, 1884
milestones.description: Kirkman, working with Tait, enumerated knots up to nine and then ten crossings, extending the first knot tables.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Trans. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh 32 (1884).
Kirkman published his first knot paper in 1884 and with Tait produced tables up to 10 crossings.

milestones.note: Tait's Part II (1884) and Part III (1886) in the same transactions also belong here; Wikipedia dates Tait's ten-crossing table to 1885. C. N. Little's 1885 role is not verified.

milestones.label: Alexander's invariants of knots and links
milestones.work: J. W. Alexander, Topological invariants of knots and links, Trans. AMS 30, 1928
milestones.description: Alexander introduced a polynomial invariant, moving knot theory from tabulation towards topology.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Trans. AMS 30 (1928).
Early 20th century topologists used the knot group and Alexander polynomial.

milestones.label: Reidemeister's Knotentheorie
milestones.work: K. Reidemeister, Knotentheorie, Ergebnisse der Mathematik, Berlin: Springer, 1932
milestones.description: A monograph giving the topological theory of knots under the name Knotentheorie.

evidence.claim: Reviews in 1933 record the 1932 Springer volume.

milestones.note: Also the title-level naming 'Knotentheorie'; 'first monograph' is not independently verified.

milestones.label: Journal of Knot Theory and Its Ramifications
milestones.work: J. Knot Theory Ramifications, vol. 1, 1992
milestones.description: A dedicated journal for the field appears.

evidence.claim: Crossref lists volume 1 (1992).

works.citation: On vortex atoms, Phil. Mag. 34
On Knots, Trans. RSE 28
Enumeration, description and construction of knots of fewer than ten crossings
Ueber Integrale der hydrodynamischen Gleichungen

notes: Tait's first printed paper is dated 1877 (Crossref) although work began earlier; Wikipedia gives 1885 for his ten-crossing table. Little's contribution (1885) is mentioned in the literature but unverified here. Naming 'knot theory' pre-dates Reidemeister (German Knotentheorie) but earlier use was not searched.

canonicalName: Beltrami and Klein models of non-Euclidean geometry

milestones.label: Cayley's projective definition of distance
milestones.work: A. Cayley, A sixth memoir upon quantics, Phil. Trans. 149, 1859
milestones.description: Cayley defined metric notions inside projective geometry via an absolute conic, the tool Klein would later use.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Phil. Trans. 1859.
Cayley's 1859 cross-ratio definition of angle became the Cayley metric.

milestones.label: Beltrami's Saggio: hyperbolic geometry on surfaces
milestones.work: E. Beltrami, Saggio di interpretazione della geometria non-euclidea, Giornale di Matematiche 6, 1868
milestones.description: Beltrami realised Lobachevsky's plane on surfaces of constant negative curvature, linking it to Riemann's geometry.

evidence.claim: The 1868 essay gives a concrete realisation using the pseudosphere.
Citation: Giornale di Matematiche 6 (1868).

milestones.note: MacTutor stresses Beltrami did not set out to prove consistency; others drew that consequence.

milestones.label: Beltrami's Teoria fondamentale: higher-dimensional and projective model
milestones.work: E. Beltrami, Teoria fondamentale degli spazii di curvatura costante, Annali di Matematica (2) 2, 1868
milestones.description: The general n-dimensional treatment, in which the model with straight lines inside a ball first appears.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Annali di Matematica 2 (1868).
The model first appeared in two 1868 memoirs of Beltrami.

milestones.label: Houel translates Beltrami and notes independence of the parallel postulate
milestones.work: J. Houel, French translations of Lobachevsky and Beltrami, 1870
milestones.description: Houel saw that Beltrami's interpretation shows the parallel postulate cannot be derived from the others.

evidence.claim: Houel translated both works in 1870 and noted the independence.

milestones.note: Dated from MacTutor only; the translation itself was not located in a bibliographic record.

milestones.label: Klein's Cayley-metric models of non-Euclidean geometry
milestones.work: F. Klein, Ueber die sogenannte Nicht-Euklidische Geometrie, Math. Ann. 4, 1871
milestones.description: Klein used Cayley's projective distance to build models of hyperbolic and elliptic geometry inside projective geometry.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Math. Ann. 4 (1871).
Klein realised Cayley's ideas give a projective model of the non-Euclidean plane.

works.citation: Teoria fondamentale degli spazii di curvatura costante
Ueber die sogenannte Nicht-Euklidische Geometrie
A sixth memoir upon quantics

notes: The summary credits Klein with the consistency proof; MacTutor says Beltrami himself did not aim at it and Houel/others drew the consequence, while Cremona delayed publication over circularity worries. Naming 'Beltrami-Klein model' is modern and undated. Klein's 1873 follow-up (Math. Ann. 6) not used as a separate milestone.

canonicalName: Tensor calculus (absolute differential calculus of Ricci and Levi-Civita)

milestones.label: Christoffel on transformation of quadratic differential forms
milestones.work: E. B. Christoffel, Ueber die Transformation der homogenen Differentialausdrucke zweiten Grades, Crelle 70, 1869
milestones.description: Christoffel solved when two quadratic differential forms are equivalent, introducing the symbols that define covariant differentiation.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Crelle 70 (1869).
Christoffel's paper was the main influence on Ricci's 1884 start; symbols fundamental in tensor analysis.

milestones.note: MacTutor's Ricci page dates the paper to 1868; Crossref gives volume year 1869.

milestones.label: Ricci's theory of quadratic differential forms
milestones.work: G. Ricci, Principii di una teoria delle forme differenziali quadratiche, Annali di Matematica 12, 1883-84
milestones.description: Ricci began his work on invariants of quadratic differential forms, the seed of the absolute differential calculus.

evidence.claim: Crossref issue date 1883 (volume 12 spans 1883-84).
Ricci began investigations on quadratic differential forms in 1884.

milestones.note: Year 1883 (record) versus 1884 (MacTutor).

milestones.label: Ricci's systematic presentation of absolute differential calculus
milestones.work: G. Ricci, paper for the 800th anniversary of the University of Bologna, 1888
milestones.description: Ricci first set out the covariant and contravariant technique systematically, completing four publications by 1892.

evidence.claim: Systematic presentation in 1888, with four publications between 1888 and 1892.

milestones.note: Wikipedia (Tensor) instead dates the original presentation to the 1892 Bull. Sci. Math. paper (vol. 16, pp. 167-189), which is the widely cited French exposition.

milestones.label: Voigt's modern use of 'tensor'
milestones.work: W. Voigt, Die fundamentalen physikalischen Eigenschaften der Krystalle in elementarer Darstellung, 1898
milestones.description: Voigt introduced the contemporary meaning of the word tensor in crystal physics; Ricci's own term was 'systems'.

evidence.claim: Crossref records the 1898 book.
The contemporary usage was introduced by Voigt in 1898.

milestones.label: Ricci and Levi-Civita, Methodes de calcul differentiel absolu
milestones.work: G. Ricci, T. Levi-Civita, Methodes de calcul differentiel absolu et leurs applications, Math. Ann. 54, 1900
milestones.description: The joint exposition that made the calculus accessible and showed applications to geometry and mechanics.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Math. Ann. 54 (1900).
Described as the 1900 classic that made tensor calculus accessible.

milestones.label: Levi-Civita's parallelism
milestones.work: T. Levi-Civita, Nozione di parallelismo in una varieta qualunque, Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo 42, 1917
milestones.description: Levi-Civita gave a geometric meaning to covariant differentiation as parallel transport on a manifold.

evidence.claim: Crossref lists vol. 42 with issued date 1916.

milestones.note: Volume year versus print year (1916/1917).

milestones.label: Einstein's general relativity written in tensor calculus
milestones.work: A. Einstein, Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitatstheorie, Ann. Phys. 354, 1916
milestones.description: Einstein's field theory made absolute differential calculus the standard language of geometry and physics.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Ann. Phys. 354 (1916).

milestones.note: The earlier Einstein-Grossmann Entwurf (1913) is the first physical use but was not verified in a record.

works.citation: Principii di una teoria delle forme differenziali quadratiche
Methodes de calcul differentiel absolu et leurs applications
Ueber die Transformation der homogenen Differentialausdrucke zweiten Grades
Die fundamentalen physikalischen Eigenschaften der Krystalle

notes: Dates for Ricci disagree between MacTutor (systematic presentation 1888) and Wikipedia (1892 Bull. Sci. Math.); the 1888 Bologna paper and the 1892 paper were not found in a bibliographic record. Riemann's 1854 lecture (published 1868) is a background precursor not listed. The Tensor milestone for naming is the modern physics sense, distinct from Hamilton's older use.

milestones.label: Lie's contact transformations and PDEs
milestones.work: S. Lie, Ueber Complexe, insbesondere Linien- und Kugel-Complexe, mit Anwendung auf die Theorie partieller Differentialgleichungen, Math. Ann. 5, 1872
milestones.description: Lie used contact transformations (found in Paris) to treat complexes and first-order partial differential equations.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Math. Ann. 5 (1872).
Contact transformations discovered in Paris; doctorate 1872.

milestones.label: Winter 1873-74: Lie starts the theory of continuous groups
milestones.description: Lie turned from PDEs to systematic work on continuous transformation groups and infinitesimal generators.

evidence.claim: Lie began developing the theory of continuous transformation groups in winter 1873-74.
Lie considered that winter the birth of the theory; Hawkins suggests a longer period.

milestones.label: Lie's Theorie der Transformationsgruppen in the Christiania archive
milestones.work: S. Lie, Theorie der Transformations-Gruppen I, II, Archiv for Mathematik og Naturvidenskab 1, 1876
milestones.description: Lie set out transformation groups and their infinitesimal generators in a Norwegian journal.

evidence.claim: Cited with pages 19-57 and 152-193, 1876.

milestones.note: An 1874 Gottingen Nachrichten note on groups of transformations probably precedes this; its original year was not confirmed (only a modern reprint record was found).

milestones.label: Theorie der Transformationsgruppen I in Math. Annalen
milestones.work: S. Lie, Theorie der Transformationsgruppen I, Math. Ann. 16, 1880
milestones.description: A major German-language account that brought the theory to a wide readership.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Math. Ann. 16 (1880).

milestones.label: Killing's classification work on finite continuous groups
milestones.work: W. Killing, Die Zusammensetzung der stetigen endlichen Transformationsgruppen, Math. Ann. 33, 1888
milestones.description: Killing began the structural classification of the algebras of continuous groups, later completed by Cartan.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Math. Ann. 33 (1888), with sequels in vols 34 and 36.

milestones.note: Significance stated from background knowledge, not read in the paper.

milestones.label: Lie and Engel, Theorie der Transformationsgruppen (three volumes)
milestones.work: S. Lie, F. Engel, Theorie der Transformationsgruppen, Leipzig: Teubner, 1888-93
milestones.description: The first systematic treatise on continuous groups, in three volumes.

evidence.claim: Archive.org record: Leipzig, Teubner, 1888-93.
Three volumes published 1888, 1890, 1893.

milestones.label: 'Groupes de Lie' first appears
milestones.work: A. Tresse, Sur les invariants differentiels des groupes continus de transformations, 1893
milestones.description: The term for Lie groups arises in French in the thesis of Lie's student Tresse.

evidence.claim: The term 'groupes de Lie' first appeared in 1893 in Tresse's thesis.

milestones.label: Weyl's representation theory of semisimple groups
milestones.work: H. Weyl, Theorie der Darstellung kontinuierlicher halb-einfacher Gruppen durch lineare Transformationen, Math. Z. 23, 1925
milestones.description: Weyl turned Lie groups into a central tool for representation theory and mathematical physics.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Math. Z. 23 (1925).

milestones.note: Significance from background knowledge.

works.citation: Theorie der Transformationsgruppen I
Theorie der Transformationsgruppen (with Lie)
Die Zusammensetzung der stetigen endlichen Transformationsgruppen
Theorie der Darstellung kontinuierlicher halb-einfacher Gruppen

notes: The first_statement is low-precision: Lie's 1874 Gottingen note and 1876 Archiv papers are both candidates and only the 1876 citation is on a history page. No first_application recorded; Lie's integration of ODEs by groups was not dated from a record. The term 'Lie algebra' (Weyl, 1930s) was not searched.

aliases: Birkhoff and von Neumann ergodic theorems

milestones.label: Koopman: Hamiltonian systems as unitary operators on Hilbert space
milestones.work: B. O. Koopman, Hamiltonian systems and transformation in Hilbert space, PNAS 17, 1931
milestones.description: Koopman represented classical flows by unitary operators on Hilbert space, the idea von Neumann then used.

evidence.claim: Crossref: PNAS 17 (1931).
Koopman's idea of operators on a function space stimulated von Neumann's ergodic theorem.

milestones.label: Birkhoff's ergodic theorem
milestones.work: G. D. Birkhoff, Proof of the ergodic theorem, PNAS 17, 1931
milestones.description: Birkhoff proved that time averages exist almost everywhere for measure-preserving flows.

evidence.claim: Crossref: PNAS 17 (1931).
The Birkhoff (1931) and von Neumann theorems are the two key ergodic theorems.

milestones.note: Priority with von Neumann (whose proof was earlier but printed in 1932) is discussed by Zund 2002, cited on the history page.

milestones.label: von Neumann's mean ergodic theorem
milestones.work: J. von Neumann, Proof of the quasi-ergodic hypothesis, PNAS 18, 1932
milestones.description: Von Neumann proved the mean ergodic theorem using Hilbert space methods, giving a rigorous basis to Boltzmann's hypothesis.

evidence.claim: Crossref: PNAS 18 (1932).
Described as the first rigorous proof of an ergodic theorem.

milestones.label: Birkhoff and Koopman survey of recent ergodic theory
milestones.work: G. D. Birkhoff, B. O. Koopman, Recent contributions to the ergodic theory, PNAS 18, 1932
milestones.description: An early survey of the new theorems and their connections.

evidence.claim: Crossref: PNAS 18 (1932).

milestones.label: Hopf's Ergodentheorie
milestones.work: E. Hopf, Ergodentheorie, Ergebnisse der Mathematik, Berlin: Springer, 1937
milestones.description: A monograph presenting the theory, including geodesic flow on surfaces of negative curvature.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Springer 1937, Ergodentheorie.

milestones.note: 'First monograph' not verified.

milestones.label: Furstenberg's ergodic proof of Szemeredi's theorem
milestones.work: H. Furstenberg, Ergodic behavior of diagonal measures and a theorem of Szemeredi on arithmetic progressions, J. Anal. Math. 31, 1977
milestones.description: Ergodic methods were used to prove a deep combinatorial theorem, extending the field's reach.

evidence.claim: Crossref: J. Analyse Math. 31 (1977).

milestones.label: Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems journal
milestones.work: Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems, vol. 1, 1981
milestones.description: A journal named after the field starts.

evidence.claim: Crossref lists volume 1 (1981).

works.citation: Proof of the ergodic theorem
Proof of the quasi-ergodic hypothesis
Hamiltonian systems and transformation in Hilbert space
Ergodentheorie

notes: Boltzmann's hypothesis is credited on the history page to his gas theory lectures (1898 Part 2, term 'Ergoden'); the earliest coinage and original 1860s-1880s papers were not verified, so no precursor or naming milestone is recorded. Birkhoff and von Neumann priority is disputed. Poincare recurrence (1890) not included.

aliases: Geometry as invariants of a group
Vergleichende Betrachtungen uber neuere geometrische Forschungen

milestones.label: Cayley: metric geometry inside projective geometry
milestones.work: A. Cayley, A sixth memoir upon quantics, Phil. Trans. 149, 1859
milestones.description: Cayley showed Euclidean metric geometry can be defined from projective geometry.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Phil. Trans. 1859.
1859 definition of distance via cross-ratio became the Cayley metric.

milestones.label: Klein's non-Euclidean models from projective geometry
milestones.work: F. Klein, Ueber die sogenannte Nicht-Euklidische Geometrie, Math. Ann. 4, 1871
milestones.description: Klein related the geometries by projective means, preparing the group-theoretic classification.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Math. Ann. 4 (1871).

milestones.label: Klein's Vergleichende Betrachtungen (Erlangen programme)
milestones.work: F. Klein, Vergleichende Betrachtungen uber neuere geometrische Forschungen, Erlangen: Deichert, 1872
milestones.description: Klein proposed classifying geometries by the group of transformations whose invariants they study.

evidence.claim: Archive.org record: Erlangen, A. Deichert, 1872.
The Erlanger Programm (1872) unified geometry as study of group invariants.

milestones.note: Written for Klein's Erlangen appointment; not the talk he gave.

milestones.label: Programme reprinted in Math. Annalen
milestones.work: F. Klein, Vergleichende Betrachtungen uber neuere geometrische Forschungen, Math. Ann. 43, 1893
milestones.description: Reprinted with a note, giving it wide circulation.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Math. Ann. 43 (1893).

milestones.note: Same text as the 1872 pamphlet.

milestones.label: English translation by Haskell
milestones.work: F. Klein (tr. M. W. Haskell), A comparative review of recent researches in geometry, Bull. NY Math. Soc. 2, 1893
milestones.description: The English translation spread the programme in the English-speaking world.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Bull. AMS (formerly Bull. NY Math. Soc.) 2 (1893).

works.citation: Vergleichende Betrachtungen uber neuere geometrische Forschungen
A sixth memoir upon quantics

notes: No first_application or naming milestone established: the name 'Erlangen programme' and the first uses of the group-classification (e.g. by Cartan, Veblen) were not dated in records. MacTutor says the programme was written for the inaugural occasion but not the talk given.

canonicalName: Derivation of the Boltzmann equation from hard-sphere dynamics
aliases: Hilbert's sixth problem for kinetic theory

milestones.label: Boltzmann's kinetic equation
milestones.work: L. Boltzmann, Weitere Studien uber das Warmegleichgewicht unter Gasmolekulen, Wiener Berichte, 1872
milestones.description: Boltzmann derived the kinetic equation for gas density from collisions, with a molecular chaos assumption.

evidence.claim: The Boltzmann equation was devised by Boltzmann in 1872.

milestones.label: Hilbert's sixth problem
milestones.work: D. Hilbert, Mathematical problems, address 1900; Bull. AMS 8, 1902
milestones.description: Hilbert asked for rigorous axiomatisation of mechanics and a treatment of kinetic gas theory limits.

evidence.claim: Hilbert's sixth problem asks for rigorous methods of mean values in kinetic gas theory.
Bull. AMS 8 (1902) English version.

milestones.note: Talk given 1900; the cited record is the 1902 translation.

milestones.label: Cercignani on the rigid-sphere Boltzmann equation
milestones.work: C. Cercignani, On the Boltzmann equation for rigid spheres, Transport Theory Statist. Phys. 2, 1972
milestones.description: A study of the Boltzmann equation for hard spheres, the model later treated by Lanford.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Transport Theory Stat. Phys. 2 (1972).

milestones.note: Relevance assessed from the title only.

milestones.label: Lanford's derivation for short times
milestones.work: O. E. Lanford, Time evolution of large classical systems, Lecture Notes in Physics 38, 1975
milestones.description: Lanford first derived the Boltzmann equation from hard-sphere Newtonian dynamics for a short fraction of a collision time.

evidence.claim: Crossref: Lecture Notes in Physics (1975).
Lanford was first to derive the equation for small times in 1975.

milestones.label: Illner and Pulvirenti: global validity for a rare gas in vacuum
